concepts.title: The Family: Basic Unit of Society
concepts.definition: The family is the fundamental and most ancient unit of society, where children are born, nurtured and taught values; Indian families range from joint households to nuclear ones.
concepts.key_idea: Society is built family by family: the first lessons of living together are learned at home.

concepts.title: Joint and Nuclear Families
concepts.definition: A joint family keeps several generations under one roof, grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts and cousins, while a nuclear family is only a couple with their children; Indian languages even name relations that English must borrow words for.
concepts.key_idea: Family shape changes but the web of relations stays dense: bua, tau, chacha and nani name bonds that matter.

concepts.title: Dharma and Values within the Family
concepts.definition: The family is a school of values where children learn ahimsa, dana, seva and tyaga; in the story, Shalini gives up her expected silk dress so the whole family can share clothes for Onam with her uncle's household.
concepts.key_idea: Following dharma in a family often means giving up a small wish so that others are not left out.

concepts.title: Community: Beyond the Family
concepts.definition: Beyond kin, people live in communities bound by place, work or faith, jatis and neighbourhoods, temples and schools; a community shares joys, helps in trouble and sets some rules of its own.
concepts.key_idea: Community extends the family's care: neighbours and fellow members become a wider circle of support.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why does the chapter call the family a school?

solution_template.explain: Ahimsa, dana, seva and tyaga are learned first at home.
In the Onam story, Shalini learns giving by watching her parents share with her uncle's family.

worked_examples.question_pattern: How does a joint family cushion a sudden loss of income?

solution_template.explain: When Shalini's uncle lost his job, the whole household adjusted its spending.
Shared income and shared needs mean one member's hardship is softened by all.
